# Driver (stage 2): IR2110 half-bridge

> English (primary) · [Русский](../../translations/ru/hardware/driver/README.md) · [Deutsch](../../translations/de/hardware/driver/README.md) · [Português](../../translations/pt/hardware/driver/README.md) · [中文](../../translations/zh/hardware/driver/README.md) · [日本語](../../translations/ja/hardware/driver/README.md)

**Schematic:** [../schematics/sch1-driver-halfbridge.png](../schematics/sch1-driver-halfbridge.png) (generated by [../schematics/render_schematics.py](../schematics/render_schematics.py))

The chain: Pi (SPI) → AD9833 **in square-wave mode** (OPBITEN bit: MSB routed to the output, rail-to-rail swing — no separate comparator needed) → **74HC14 + RC + 1N4148** shaper (complementary HIN/LIN with ~1 µs dead time) → IR2110 → 2×IRF540 (half-bridge) → 1 µF DC-blocking cap → matching transformer (ferrite, ~1:3..1:5, tune on the bench) → Langevin transducer TX.

The AD9833's sine output (~0.6 Vpp) is no good for the IR2110 logic — if for some reason you specifically need a sine out of the DDS, put a comparator between them (e.g. an LM393, not in the BOM).

Power stage supply: 12–24 V bench PSU with current limiting (**start at 0.2 A**).

Note: the stage-1 sweep drives the piezo directly with the weak DDS sine (~0.6 Vpp, see `sweep_map.py`) — **this driver enters the chain only at stage 2 (watts)**. Do not expect ≥0.5 W from the stage-1 DDS-only hookup.

Notes:
- The Langevin transducer is a capacitive load (typically a few nF). A series inductor or matching transformer is mandatory; without it the MOSFETs dissipate the reactive current and cook.
- **Matching transformer (the usual failure point).** Start with a small ferrite toroid (e.g. FT50-43 / similar), primary a few turns, secondary ~3–5× that, series DC-block 1 µF film on the primary. Tune for minimum PSU current *at the stage-1 resonance* with the TX **clamped to the plate** and the RX loaded. Turns ratio and leakage are empirical — the schematic marks them `*` for a reason. Record final turns in the experiment log.
- **Dead time**: the IR2110 does not generate it on its own. The discrete-parts option — RC+1N4148 on the 74HC14 inputs (delays rising edges only, ~1 µs; with a 25 µs period at 40 kHz that's <5% loss). The easy option — an EGS002 module, everything is built in there.
- **3.3 V logic**: power the IR2110's VDD from the same 3.3 V as the AD9833 and 74HC14 — at VDD=5 V the VIH threshold is ≈ 3.1 V and a 3.3 V square wave barely squeaks through (the datasheet allows VDD down to 3.3 V).
- **Decoupling is mandatory**: 100 nF at VDD and VCC (VCC — plus 47 µF), and on the power rail 470–1000 µF + 100 nF ceramic right at the half-bridge legs — without this, a half-bridge on breadboard jumpers picks up its own switching spikes. Keep power-loop wires short; if the switch node rings badly, move off the breadboard to a copper-clad dead-bug / protoboard ground pour before raising current.
- **First power-up sequence** (aligned with [docs/02-safety.md](../../docs/02-safety.md)):
  1. No Langevin on the secondary yet. PSU = 12 V, current limit 0.2 A. Scope gate drive (HIN/LIN) and switch node — confirm dead time and no shoot-through.
  2. Fit the matching transformer + TX Langevin **clamped to the steel plate** (or a thick sacrificial metal block). Still 0.2 A limit. Bring up at the stage-1 peak frequency only long enough to see current and RX voltage.
  3. Raise the current limit gradually while watching MOSFET and transformer temperature. Never leave an unclamped Langevin at power — free-air full-power runs are how ceramics crack and drivers die.
